subsections.title: Government Structure
subsections.content: São Tomé and Príncipe operates a semi-presidential multi-party democratic system. The President is elected for two five-year terms, while the Prime Minister, appointed by the President, holds most executive powers. Governments are often short-lived due to coalition politics. Civil liberties are generally respected, though institutional weaknesses and corruption affect governance.

subsections.title: Trade Environment
subsections.content: The country is not yet a member of the WTO, limiting its integration into global trade systems. Trade is highly concentrated with Europe, particularly Portugal. Imports significantly exceed exports, creating a persistent trade deficit. The economy depends heavily on imported goods and a narrow export base focused on cocoa.

subsections.title: Tax Policies
subsections.content: São Tomé and Príncipe has a developing tax system with a 10% VAT and progressive income tax rates up to 25%. While tax incentives exist for investors, weak administrative capacity and a large informal sector reduce tax efficiency.

subsections.title: Political Challenges
subsections.content: The country faces governance challenges including limited transparency, weak enforcement of laws, corruption, and a large informal sector. Media independence is constrained and access to public information is limited.

subsections.title: Political Stability
subsections.content: Despite past instability, the country has experienced peaceful democratic transitions. However, coalition governments and institutional capacity issues continue to pose risks.

subsections.title: Inflation
subsections.content: Inflation remains relatively high but is declining, reaching around 9–10% in 2026. Historically, inflation has been volatile, affecting purchasing power and economic stability.

subsections.title: Interest Rate
subsections.content: Interest rates are relatively high at around 10%, reflecting efforts to control inflation. However, this limits access to financing and reduces private sector investment.

subsections.title: Exchange Rate
subsections.content: The local currency (STN) is pegged to the euro, providing monetary stability but limiting policy flexibility. The economy relies heavily on foreign reserves.

subsections.title: Economic Growth
subsections.content: Economic growth remains modest (around 1.7%) and below historical averages. The economy is small and heavily dependent on agriculture, tourism, and foreign aid.

subsections.title: Unemployment
subsections.content: Unemployment averages around 9–10%, but a large informal sector dominates the labor market, reducing job stability and productivity.

subsections.title: Demographics
subsections.content: The population is approximately 247,000, with steady annual growth of about 2%. The country has a young and expanding population.

subsections.title: Population Structure
subsections.content: Around 38–42% of the population is under 15 years old, indicating a high dependency ratio and strong demand for education and employment opportunities.

subsections.title: Culture and Lifestyle
subsections.content: The country follows a relaxed 'Leve Leve' lifestyle, emphasizing simplicity and community. Culture is influenced by African and Portuguese traditions.

subsections.title: Education
subsections.content: Primary education enrollment is high, and literacy rates have improved. However, challenges remain in secondary education completion and overall quality.

subsections.title: Consumer Behavior
subsections.content: Consumers prioritize essential goods due to low income levels and high reliance on imports. Informal markets dominate purchasing habits.

subsections.title: Healthcare
subsections.content: Healthcare infrastructure is limited, with only one main hospital. Patients often travel abroad for advanced treatment.

subsections.title: Technology in Education
subsections.content: Technology adoption in education is limited but improving through international initiatives and digital learning programs.

subsections.title: Infrastructure Challenges
subsections.content: The country faces limited internet access, lack of devices, and insufficient ICT training for teachers.

subsections.title: Digital Adoption
subsections.content: Mobile penetration is relatively strong, with over 60% of the population connected. Internet usage is growing but remains uneven across regions.

subsections.title: Digital Limitations
subsections.content: Digital infrastructure remains weak, especially in rural areas, limiting full participation in the digital economy.

subsections.title: Environmental Overview
subsections.content: São Tomé and Príncipe is a small island developing state vulnerable to climate change, coastal erosion, and environmental degradation.

subsections.title: Climate Risks
subsections.content: The country faces sea-level rise, flooding, and extreme weather events, which impact agriculture, infrastructure, and livelihoods.

subsections.title: Adaptation Efforts
subsections.content: Government and international partners are implementing coastal protection, flood management, and climate-resilient infrastructure projects.

subsections.title: Legal System
subsections.content: The legal system is based on Portuguese law and includes constitutional, administrative, and ordinary courts. It supports rule of law but faces enforcement challenges.

subsections.title: Investment Laws
subsections.content: Investment regulations promote foreign investment through incentives, equal treatment, and protection against expropriation.

subsections.title: Land Regulations
subsections.content: Most land is state-owned. Foreign investors can access land through concession systems rather than ownership.

subsections.title: Labor and Residency Laws
subsections.content: Foreign workers must meet quotas and secure permits. Residency visas are available for work, study, and investment purposes.

subsections.title: Religious Freedom
subsections.content: The constitution guarantees freedom of religion and separation of state and religion, with equal rights for all groups.
